we have been able to achieve our pedagogical objectives of teaching students to be more sensitive to the lives of their clients and more effective in representing their clients' interests.

the integration of critical theory into our clinical seminar has enhanced our students' abilities to identify and analyze power relationships in the lives of their clients and in the lawyering process; has enabled our students to develop an appreciation for and sensitivity to the impact of power on their clients' lives; has helped our students to develop a more sophisticated understanding of the law; and has helped our students develop more sophisticated lawyering skills and more effective client relationships.

critical theory is an effective tool in teaching students to deconstruct the assumptions they make about their clients and their lives, to identify the presence and importance in the client's life of alternative voices that may be invisible, and to recognize the systemic impact of the client's problems on the client, the legal system, and society.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of critical theory in clinical education is a powerful tool for helping students develop the skills and values necessary to become effective lawyers.

the infusion of critical theory into the clinic is a useful and important way to achieve our goals of helping students develop critical thinking and lawyering skills and to prepare students to be competent and effective advocates.
infusion of critical legal theory into the curriculum of the clinical education is not just a good idea, but an essential component of a successful clinical program.
